question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Trendline of a Given Scatter Plot
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/294e45be62260374df597915428bf83ac676ce709d727a7d194755cb73d78b72.png)

The scatter plot above shows the correspondence between the distance of a house from the nearest public transport facility and its price, in thousands of dollars, among a sample of newly built homes. Which of the following is the trend line of the scatter plot?
question.worked_solution:
The plot shows that the data points are scattered along a curve, not a straight line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/e4654e24215c05554c4985cccc2dcce5f6579de537a6218f4b859f13ff276a29.png)

Therefore, there is no linear trend in the data.

choices.value: There is no linear trend in the data

answer_fields.correct_value: There is no linear trend in the data

evidence.value: There is no linear trend in the data
evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, there is no linear trend in the data.

question.knowledge_point: Determining the Equation of a Trendline
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/1c9f30692222eaaed4cda6b608dcc1ccb01eefd6b5fa7730b5b8bb29c9f528b1.png)

Determine the equation of the trend line shown above.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,2)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(7,8).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{8-2}{7-2} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=\frac{6}{5}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=\frac{6}{5}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{6}{5}x+b \\ 2 & =\frac{6}{5}(2)+b \\ 2 & =\frac{12}{5}+b \\ 10 & =12+5b \\ -2 & =5b \\ b & =-\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=\frac{6}{5}x-\frac{2}{5}.
$$

evidence.solution_quote:
Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$

$$

question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/31394106551498e7fd3a5cf57773f11ae31c7bc80c9a12272e95033bdcfd462e.png)

Determine the equation of the trend line shown above.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the trend line passes through the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(0,9)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(7,3).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we compute the slope $m$ of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{3-9}{7-0} \\  & =\frac{-6}{7} \\  & =-\frac{6}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-\frac{6}{7}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-\frac{6}{7}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(0,9):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{6}{7}x+b \\ 9 & =-\frac{6}{7}(0)+b \\ 9 & =0+b \\ b & =9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-\frac{6}{7}x+9.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-\frac{6}{7}x+9.
$$

question.knowledge_point: Estimating the Equation of a Trendline
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/111833881cf8e939d896f23a5ab7ca436f9265e7b8fd66c099eb118eab8fd6b0.png)

Estimate the equation of the trend line for the scatter plot above. Round both the slope and the $y$-intercept to the nearest $0.5.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's draw an approximate trend line for our scatter plot:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938989/assets/fdad2c939372e14617ba4e393037d7f5852cd8114467aa914ccb8963c0eacfeb.png)

It seems that the trend line passes through $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})≈(2,5)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})≈(6,1).$

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

First, we estimate the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ≈\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{1-5}{6-2} \\  & =\frac{-4}{4} \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $m=-1$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-x+b.
$$

We now need to estimate the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can do this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(2,5):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-x+b \\ 5 & =-2+b \\ 7 & =b \\ b & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-x+7.
$$

evidence.solution_quote:
Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-x+7.
$$
